reviews.review:
The First Descendant pleasantly surprised me. The gameplay is smooth and satisfying, and unlocking new Descendants and upgrading them gives a constant sense of progression.
The graphics are excellent, and the combat effects look impressive. The co-op is also very fun and makes missions more dynamic.
It requires some grinding, but it’s part of the experience and doesn’t feel frustrating. If you like looter shooters like Warframe or Destiny, it’s definitely worth trying.

Crowded UI both in game and the shop, confusing icons, and endless amounts of weapons that are all similar yet slightly different. This game is constant visual overload to the point of anxiety. A cool concept that fails to keep me playing and makes me feel stressed -- and not in a rewarding way. 

There are games like project zomboid that do everything in its power to make the game harder for the player, and even tell the player upfront that they will lose in the end, but is still engaging enough to make you want to keep coming back. None of the missions in TFD make me excited, and I find myself here just to try and unlock characters just to waste hours a day not even getting close. If you're going to force players to basically take on the same task for hours on end just to maybe get closer to getting materials for a character, at least bring some variety to it. No matter who I play as I find I can play this game just shooting my gun and never relying on any of the character abilities, and that's kind of a shame. 

As for the characters; If you're a person like me and cool and attractive characters catch your attention, there are also much better places to find that with more meaningful gameplay experiences. While the Dead or Alive and Soul Calibur series is in the fighting genre, I find those games to satisfy the itch that this game is trying to scratch.

The enemies in this game are repetitive, the characters have way too many abilities, and the central hub world feels both crowded and small all at the same time. Navigating the world is both confusing, boring, and stressful. It feels like a day job made for people with chronic ADHD that need to work on something but don't have the confidence to go out in the real world. I feel like I'm falling into a void when I play this. 

Trust me -- a day job I mildly dislike is much more rewarding than this game. I really, really wanted to like this game but just can't bring myself to.

Played previously on xbox, had a good start and fun co-op gameplay, before updates turned the game into a solo grind with useless co-op mechanics. Cross progression is dead coz of dumb account linking system, worst I've seen so far.
